settings.heading: Selecting the wood
settings.body: Every top starts as a single board, tapped and listened to before it's ever cut. We're listening for stiffness, for resonance, for the wood's own voice — the instrument's tone is decided here, months before assembly begins.

settings.heading: Shaping by hand
settings.body: Braces are carved and tuned by ear, not machine. The body is bent, glued, and clamped using techniques that haven't changed much in a century — because they still work better than anything faster.

settings.heading: The final finish
settings.body: A thin, hand-rubbed finish that lets the wood keep breathing. Every instrument is strung, set up, and played by the luthier who built it before it's ever offered for sale.

settings.name: Owen Marsh
settings.quote: I still tap every top myself before it's cut. Some habits you don't automate.

settings.name: Dana Kessler
settings.quote: The finish is the last thing anyone touches before it leaves. It has to be right.

settings.name: Théo Abara
settings.quote: Half my week is new builds, the other half is fixing instruments twice my age.
